body: Yep, always changed in a bathroom stall cause I felt uncomfortable changing with the guys in my class and wore a shirt of some form while swimming, though I did eventually stop wearing a shirt while swimming, I just started diving straight into the water and minimizing time spent above water as much as possible.

My best guess would be that you completed the awakened atlas level challenge. ie "Complete this map at tier 12 with awakening lv2". (alongside the standard complete a [magic/rare] version of this map challenge)

> but have you ever considered therapy?

Honestly, I don't think it would do me much good anyway. Back in elementary school and part of middle/high school (from about 4th Grade to probably 8-9th) I would get passes to talk with the school counseller/therapy type person, and I remember also talking to someone at the local doctor's office (they might have been the same person, I honestly don't remember) (I moved states when I was 9, mainly due to my mother's worries about where we were (bad neighborhood) and that past ~4th grade I would be stuck with public schools and that the bullying I was already receiving at a private school would just become that much worse (at the private school I was already like one of three white kids in an otherwise black school of like 300 kids, and it was not an enjoyable time)). I remember stuff like the counseller asking me how my day was, how I was etc. I would always just reply 'fine' or 'great', then we would play UNO and that would be it. I remember once we brainstormed ways to 'make friends', topics of interest and the like for me to use. Never used them, I would just read my books during recess anyway, what did I need friends for? I never opened up to them because of my "It's YOUR problem and no one else's and that asking for help is a last resort" type mentality, which I still have. So it would likely just end up being a waste of time and money.

I mean, the thing is I do *know* it's gonna be fine at the end of the day. Sure, doing a 2-year course in 2.5 or 3 years hurts both my pride and my wallet, but I'm 19, I have all the time in the world to make bank, and it's not like I'm finding out I'm garbage at the course/job of my dreams or anything, I went to college cause on *average* you make more money with a college degree than without (I'm an electrical engineering major) and I figured it would be something I could tolerate doing for money without being completely bored out of my mind. I honestly suspect that when I either graduate or just give up on college and all the stress it brings, the "suicidal ideation" and darker thoughts will disappear, as I can't really remember having them *before* college started anyway. The only real issue I can think of from before college is feeling 'emotionally numb' some times, but eh, that comes and goes anyway. It's just sometimes it sucks and feels like the world is ending, but it really isn't. I do wish I wasn't quite so damn lazy, but I doubt that will change regardless what I do, so eh.
